instruction: Create a simple bash monitoring script
Set up a dead man's switch cron
Monitor a log file for specific keywords and alert

output:
apt install -y monit && cat > /etc/monit/conf.d/nginx << 'EOF'
check process nginx with pidfile /run/nginx.pid
  start program = "/usr/sbin/nginx"
  stop program = "/usr/sbin/nginx -s stop"
  if failed port 80 protocol http then restart
  if 5 restarts within 5 cycles then timeout
EOF && monit reload && monit start nginx

gem install god && cat > /etc/god/conf.god << 'EOF'
God.watch do |w|
  w.name = "nginx"
  w.start = "nginx"
  w.restart = "nginx -s reload"
  w.keepalive
end
EOF && god start
apt install -y supervisor && systemctl enable --now supervisor

cat > /etc/supervisor/conf.d/myapp.conf << 'EOF'
[program:myapp]
command=/usr/local/bin/myapp
user=john
autostart=true
autorestart=true
stderr_logfile=/var/log/myapp.err.log
stdout_logfile=/var/log/myapp.out.log
EOF && supervisorctl update

instruction: Check if any service is consuming too much memory
output: ps aux --sort=-%mem | awk 'NR>1{if($4>10) print $11" uses "$4"% memory"}'

instruction: Check if any process is using swap heavily
output: for f in /proc/*/status; do awk '/VmSwap|Name/{printf "%s ", $2} END {print ""}' $f 2>/dev/null; done | sort -k2 -rh | head -10
